authority: apostila-cga-2026; elliptical-coordination sweep over all 28 compound families in the registry
method: every `HEAD de X <conj> Y` in the corpus where `HEAD de Y` is also a registered form, enumerated and each resolution checked by execution
reason: A review found `risco de mercado e liquidez` resolving `liquidez` to the property when the shared head makes it the RISK, called the residual 2-3 occurrences, and asked whether it deserves an engine mechanism for head propagation across coordination. Measured rather than argued: 28 compound families, 6 coordinations in the whole corpus, 5 with an unresolved second conjunct, 4 of them resolving to a confidently WRONG concept. Four occurrences in 7836 events does not justify teaching the matcher syntax it does not have — but confidently wrong is worse for a consumer than unmatched, and that part is fixable with no architecture at all. Each collocation below occurs exactly once, so blocking it costs no correct match; the span becomes unresolved, which is the honest state for something the engine cannot read.

operations.why: `Principais fatores de risco: risco de mercado e liquidez` and `Exemplos: risco de crédito ou de liquidez de uma companhia` — the head `risco de` governs both conjuncts, so the second is liquidity RISK, not liquidity. Each string occurs once. A third: `Inclui risco de mercado, de crédito, operacional, de liquidez, entre outros` coordinates four members under one head and the last one is far enough from it that blocking the pair before it does not reach — also one occurrence.
`risco de mercado ou de crédito` and `risco de mercado, de crédito, operacional, de liquidez` — same shared head, and `crédito` alone reads as the entity. Each string occurs once.
